summary: E2E browser verification of the security hardening package (login+2FA, password change, activity log, logout-everywhere, honeypot, headers) plus regressions (registrations, contact, pagination, admin tabs). All 7 target flows work. Discovered ONE minor UI regression: 2FA status badge in Security tab is stale immediately after a fresh 2FA sign-in — a reload fixes it.

minor.issue: Response payloads omit `totp_enabled`. /auth/me returns it (line 145) but the two login endpoints return only {id,email,role} (server.py lines 838, 879). Frontend SecurityTab reads user.totp_enabled to render the Enabled/Not-enabled badge and the setup-vs-disable form → wrong state until a page reload.

ui_bugs.issue: After a successful password+TOTP login the badge shows 'Not enabled' and the 'Set up 2FA' button appears, even though 2FA is active on the server. Reload resolves it. Root cause: /auth/login/2fa response is missing totp_enabled (see backend minor issue). Also — if the user clicks 'Set up 2FA' from this stale state, the backend correctly rejects with 400 'already enabled'.

action_items: Minor: Add `totp_enabled` (and any other user fields SecurityTab reads) to the JSON returned by POST /api/auth/login and POST /api/auth/login/2fa, or have SecurityTab re-fetch /auth/me after mount. Also consider having /auth/2fa/activate/disable return the updated user so state stays authoritative.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: /auth/login and /auth/login/2fa hand-craft the user response and drift from /auth/me — extract a shared serialize_user(user) helper so all three endpoints return the same shape (id, email, role, totp_enabled).
Register.jsx / Contact.jsx: honeypot is `class=hidden` — good — but for stronger bot resistance consider also `tabindex=-1 autocomplete=off aria-hidden=true` on the input.

SecurityTab TwoFactorCard initialises enabled=!!user?.totp_enabled once and only ever mutates it via activate/disable success; if user prop updates (e.g. after refresh) the local state won't sync. A `useEffect(()=>setEnabled(!!user?.totp_enabled),[user?.totp_enabled])` would keep them in step.
server.py /admin/login-events has no pagination or size cap — could grow unbounded and dump the whole collection to admins. Consider `.limit(200)` + `sort({created_at:-1})`.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Everything is in the original clean state: 3 real registrations, 2 real contact messages, 8 real notices (pinned District Trials first), admin 2FA disabled, admin password CAPadmin#2026, editor Editor@123. token_version has been bumped a few times by the change-password/logout-all flow — this is expected and does not affect cred validity. The only outstanding item is the minor stale-badge UI issue on the Security tab immediately after a 2FA-enabled login.
rca of the issue: SecurityTab reads user.totp_enabled from the prop passed by <Admin/>. That prop is set from the /auth/login (or /auth/login/2fa) response, which returns only {id,email,role} while /auth/me returns totp_enabled too. Consequence: right after a fresh 2FA login, the state object in the parent is missing totp_enabled, so `enabled = !!user?.totp_enabled` is false and the badge/CTA render as if 2FA were off. A reload triggers /auth/me and the state becomes correct. Fix path: (a) include totp_enabled in the two login response payloads OR (b) call /auth/me right after onSuccess to backfill the user object OR (c) sync SecurityTab local enabled state via useEffect on user.totp_enabled.
